cosy-lesson.title: The 4-Day Work Week: Productivity vs. Tradition

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Burnout – physical or mental collapse caused by overwork or stress.

p.em: Example: Many employees are suffering from burnout due to long hours.

cosy-blockquote.p: Productivity – the effectiveness of productive effort, as measured by the rate of output per unit of input.

p.em: Example: Studies show that shorter weeks can actually increase productivity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Well-being ≠ suffering – the state of being comfortable, healthy, or happy.

p.em: Example: Employee well-being should be a priority for every company.

cosy-blockquote.p: Retention – the ability of a company to keep its employees.

p.em: Example: A 4-day week can significantly improve staff retention.

cosy-blockquote.p: Overhead – the regular costs of running a business (rent, electricity, etc.).

p.em: Example: Closing the office for an extra day can reduce overhead costs.

cosy-blockquote.p: Flexibility – the quality of bending easily or being easily modified.

p.em: Example: Modern workers value flexibility more than a high salary.

cosy-blockquote.p: Trial – a formal test of something, typically in a workplace or laboratory.

p.em: Example: The government is launching a national trial of the 4-day week.

cosy-blockquote.p: Output – the amount of something produced by a person, machine, or industry.

p.em: Example: Managers should focus on output rather than hours spent at a desk.

cosy-blockquote.p: Commute – the journey between home and work.

p.em: Example: A shorter work week means one less day of stressful commuting.

cosy-blockquote.p: Implementation – the process of putting a decision or plan into effect.

p.em: Example: The implementation of the new schedule took several months.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
A: A 4-day work week significantly reduces professional burnout. B: A 5-day week distributes tasks over more days, preventing daily exhaustion.
★ Have you ever suffered from work-related burnout, and how did you recover?

A: Shorter working weeks increase overall productivity because employees waste less time. B: A 5-day week ensures constant availability for clients.
★ Do you feel your personal productivity is higher when you have a structured schedule?

A: An extra day off directly improves mental well-being and reduces stress. B: A standard 5-day routine provides stable habits that support physical health.
★ What activities contribute most to your personal well-being during the weekend?

A: Offering 4-day schedules dramatically boosts staff retention. B: Traditional schedules ensure predictable staffing and corporate stability.
★ Would the promise of a 4-day week influence your choice to stay with a company, affecting employee retention?

A: Closing the office for an extra day reduces corporate overhead costs like electricity. B: Spreading operations over 5 days maximizes the value of office lease investments.
★ Do you think cutting corporate overhead is a good enough reason to work from home?

A: Employees love the extreme flexibility of a three-day weekend. B: Fixed schedules make planning meetings and collaborative teamwork much simpler.
★ How much flexibility do you currently have in your working hours?

A: Starting a 4-day trial allows the company to test results safely. B: Consistent long-term schedules are safer for business than constant trials.
★ Would you like to participate in a temporary trial of a shorter work week?

A: It forces managers to focus on results and output rather than hours spent at a desk. B: Physical presence for 5 days maximizes opportunities for creative collaboration.
★ Is your job performance measured by your physical hours or by your actual output?

A: Eliminating one working day reduces weekly commute stress and carbon emissions. B: Spreading travel over 5 days makes public transport schedules more predictable.
★ How long is your daily commute, and does it drain your energy?

A: The successful implementation of a 4-day week modernizes the company. B: Changing established working models requires expensive and risky operational implementation.
★ What challenges would you expect during the implementation of a 4-day schedule in your workplace?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
A: Compressing 40 hours into 4 days can increase daily burnout and fatigue. B: Working 5 days keeps the daily hours short and manageable.
★ Do you think working 10 hours a day would cause you greater burnout than working 8 hours?

A: A shorter week might harm national productivity in sectors like healthcare. B: Forcing people to work 5 days leads to 'presenteeism' where actual productivity drops.
★ In your opinion, does working longer hours always result in lower productivity?

A: An extra day off might lead to unhealthy habits, reducing overall physical well-being. B: Relentless 5-day schedules leave zero time for self-care and mental well-being.
★ How does a long working week impact your physical and emotional well-being?

A: High employee turnover occurs when 4-day compressed hours harm staff retention. B: Failing to offer modern schedules causes companies to lose talent, destroying long-term retention.
★ Have you ever left a job because the rigid schedule affected your personal life and retention?

A: Businesses might face higher overhead if they have to hire extra staff to cover Fridays. B: Keeping offices open 5 days a week increases unnecessary building overhead.
★ Do you think business owners worry more about staff happiness or monthly overhead?

A: Extreme flexibility can lead to chaotic schedules where nobody is available. B: Standard 5-day schedules offer no flexibility for emergencies.
★ When a schedule lacks flexibility, how do you handle unexpected personal events?

A: A failed 4-day trial can damage company culture and client trust. B: Refusing to start a simple trial keeps the company stuck in outdated habits.
★ Why do you think some traditional managers are afraid to launch a 4-day trial?

A: Measuring performance strictly by output might create a high-pressure environment. B: Focusing on hours instead of output rewards slow and lazy working habits.
★ Do you prefer a relaxed environment or one focused strictly on high output?

A: An extra day off might encourage people to travel more, increasing leisure commute emissions. B: Forcing employees to commute every day causes unnecessary highway congestion.
★ Would you accept a lower salary if it meant you did not have to commute at all?

A: The chaotic implementation of a 4-day week could cause a temporary drop in service quality. B: Refusing the implementation of modern schedules makes a country less competitive globally.
★ Do you think the implementation of a 4-day week is inevitable in the future?

ul.li: Incorrect: I'm working in this company since 2010 → Correct: I've been working at this company since 2010 ((Present Perfect Continuous))
Incorrect: I suggest to reduce hours → Correct: I suggest reducing hours ((Suggest + -ing))
Incorrect: It is depend on the industry → Correct: It depends on the industry ((Depends as a verb))
Incorrect: The most of employees like it → Correct: Most employees like it ((Generalization))

Incorrect: I am looking forward to meet my new manager → Correct: I am looking forward to meeting my new manager ((The preposition 'to' in 'look forward to' requires a gerund/noun phrase, not an infinitive))
